text:
kevin: RFC: proposal to add an eviction-probe + graceful-drain path for spot GPU nodes. Goal is fewer cold starts and less lost work when AWS signals termination. Plan: TF changes to add an ASG lifecycle hook + SNS -> SSM runbook to drain pods, tag convention for spot-watch, and a canary rollout. thoughts?

maya: love this. rough TF prototype below, we can iterate. idea is hook -> SNS -> lambda/SSM. keeping heartbeat so heavy batches can flush.
```hcl
resource "aws_autoscaling_lifecycle_hook" "spot_eviction" {
  name                   = "spot-eviction-probe"
  autoscaling_group_name = aws_autoscaling_group.gpu_asg.name
  default_result         = "ABANDON"
  heartbeat_timeout      = 300
  lifecycle_transition   = "autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING"
  notification_target_arn= aws_sns_topic.lifecycle.arn
}
```

ash: couple notes — use mixed_instances_policy with instance weighting instead of flat instance type lists. e.g. prefer g4dn.xlarge (weight 1) -> g5.2xlarge (weight 2) -> p3.2xlarge (weight 4) so the scheduler can pick cheaper combos. also: add a metric for preempted-hours to the cost dashboard, otherwise this will hide as normal terminations.

lina: AMI/agent: make sure the drain helper is baked into the AMI userdata and we have an SSM document id referenced in TF so the lifecycle hook can call it. also suggest tagging nodes: "spot-watch=enabled" and "eviction-handler=ssm-v1" so ops can filter.

infra-oncall: what about edge cases where drain exceeds heartbeat? GPUs can time out draining long jobs. recommend heartbeat_timeout = 600 for GPU pools and a fallback that force-terminates after X minutes and requeues work. plus alert if lifecycle hook retried >3 times.

deploy-bot: CI: terraform plan for module/spot-eviction passed on branch kevin/spot-eviction (build #1234) :white_check_mark:

kevin: great feedback. i'll open the PR with: (1) lifecycle hook + SNS topic + SSM runbook reference, (2) tag convention, (3) mixed_instances_policy example, (4) canary var to enable in eu-west-1 test pool only. @maya can you add the runbook doc under ops/runbooks and include expected drain behaviors for tf rollout? I'll attach a short cost estimate (expected +2-4% infra cost but ~30% fewer lost job replays). :thumbsup:

maya: yes, will add the runbook and a small playbook for oncall. canary sounds good.

kevin: OK. filing PR and scheduling a quick sync Friday to walk through. thanks all.
